subject: 5065428F8D47E024C04F5AB4E31112CA
introduction: These prayers do not pretend. “The horizons have been straitened for me, and the doors of hope have been shut.” They state the distress, ask that it be removed, and ask for patience meanwhile; several were written by Bahá’u’lláh for others to say in His name about His own sufferings. The psalms of complaint are their closest kin, and the first prayer here echoes the twenty-second. Jesus in Gethsemane asked that the cup pass; Paul asked three times and received another answer; the Qur’an promises that “with hardship goeth ease” and that no soul is tasked beyond its scope. James’s “count it all joy” is the harder teaching.
questions: These prayers complain. Is complaint a form of faith?
What is the difference between asking for relief and refusing the trial?
Paul’s request was declined. How do the prayers prepare a person for that answer?

outside.why: Be Thou not far from me, for tribulation upon tribulation has gathered. The Psalm it echoes begins: my God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me? why art thou so far from helping me?
Have mercy upon my solitude. Lover and friend hast thou put far from me, and mine acquaintance into darkness.
The doors of hope have been shut. How long wilt thou forget me, O Lord? for ever?
Save me from the depths of the seas of tribulation. Out of the depths have I cried unto thee, O Lord.
Their keys are in Thy hands. Knock, and it shall be opened unto you.
Remove our difficulties. Cast thy burden upon the Lord, and he shall sustain thee.
The Remover of every anguish and Dispeller of every affliction. The Qur’an’s promise: but lo! with hardship goeth ease.
The Name through which sorrow is transformed into joy. Weeping may endure for a night, but joy cometh in the morning.
What has befallen the Wronged One. O my Father, if it be possible, let this cup pass from me: nevertheless not as I will, but as thou wilt.
Deliver me. Paul asked three times that his thorn be taken away, and was told: my grace is sufficient for thee. These prayers ask plainly for relief. What do they do when relief does not come?
Deliver us from all temptations and tests. Lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil.
The Ark of Thy Cause upon the seas. He arose, and rebuked the wind, and said unto the sea, peace, be still.
“Thee do we worship and Thine aid we seek.” Allah tasketh not a soul beyond its scope.

Be patient, then beseech God to remove our anguish. James goes further than patience: count it all joy when ye fall into divers temptations. Is it more honest to ask that a trial end, or to rejoice in it?
Think about their afflictions, that every affliction becomes easy. Consider him that endured, lest ye be wearied and faint in your minds.
O my Lord, the Mighty, the Loving. All things work together for good to them that love God.

shortfall: The remaining prayers repeat the cry for relief and the request for endurance.
